harmonization.label: Rock
harmonization.description: Power chords with classic-rock moves like the ♭VII. The backing band chugs them in eighth notes.

changes: Ends by walking down the home chord to C4.
Built on the C minor pentatonic, played in one hand position around frets 8–11.
Odd bars follow the shape of your tune; even bars answer it — the call-and-answer of a real solo.
Every technique is switched on, whatever your level.
Bends (b): push the string towards the ceiling until it sounds like the note shown — use two or three fingers together.
Slides (/): keep pressing and glide your finger up the string to the new fret.
Bend and release (b…r): bend up, then let the string come back down while it rings.
Vibrato (~): rock the bend a tiny bit up and down to make a held note sing.
This part sits higher up the neck than the easy solo, but your hand stays put around fret 8.

guide.title: Power chords
guide.body: Rock rhythm guitar plays just the root and fifth of each chord with distortion. Without a 3rd, the chord is neither happy nor sad — just heavy.

guide.title: The ♭VII chord
guide.body: Borrowing the chord a whole step below home (B♭ in C) gives the classic rock sound of songs that move I – ♭VII – IV.

guide.title: Pentatonic box
guide.body: Most rock solos live in the five-note minor pentatonic 'box'. Over a major key it gives a bluesy edge, especially when you bend the ♭3 up towards the 3rd.

guide.title: Bends and vibrato
guide.body: Rock lead players bend the 4th up to the 5th and the ♭7 up to the root, then hold the note with vibrato to make it sing.
